linkAbortSignal(source,target) returns a no-op unlink when source is absent or already aborted; an already aborted source immediately aborts target with source.reason. Otherwise it installs a once-only abort listener and returns an explicit removal closure. operationSignal returns the supplied signal by identity or a fresh AbortController signal; it creates no timeout or implicit cancellation scope. raceWithAbort returns the original promise unchanged when there is no signal. With a pre-aborted signal it attaches a rejection observer to the operation before returning a rejection, so later operation failure is consumed. With a live signal it creates one settled flag, installs a once-only listener, registers operation fulfillment/rejection, and rechecks aborted after registration to close the setup window. Whichever callback wins removes the listener; later callbacks cannot change the result. The abort result is signal.reason unless undefined, in which case it uses a DOMException with name AbortError. Loaded native files are quarantined under the nearest node_modules directory before a TS package self-update. Later startup attempts best-effort removal of that quarantine, while individual moves preserve a copy at the original package location.

normalizePath applies resolve then toNamespacedPath. getQuarantineRoot walks upward from the package directory until basename lowercased equals node_modules, returning <node_modules>/.ice-native-quarantine; reaching the filesystem root returns undefined. getLoadedSharedObjects reads process.report.getReport().sharedObjects, returns [] unless an array, ignores nonstrings, normalizes each path and its package root, compares them lowercased, keeps only getCwdRelativePath-contained files, and deduplicates case-insensitively while returning the normalized original spelling (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/windows-self-update.ts:1-46).

cleanupWindowsNativeQuarantine returns if no root and recursively force-removes the complete quarantine root, swallowing removal errors. quarantineWindowsNativeDependencies returns if no root or no loaded files; otherwise it creates a unique <Date.now>-<pid>-<randomUUID> run directory. In report order, still-existing loaded files are moved to the same package-relative destination under that run after recursive parent creation, then copied back to the original location. Rename/copy failure propagates; there is no per-file rollback or finally. A failure after rename can therefore leave a moved file without its replacement. This is the source's mutation ordering, not an executed Windows failure (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/windows-self-update.ts:48-84).

The helper itself has no platform guard. Main invokes cleanup only on win32; explicit self-update invocation is CLI-038. No direct helper test was found by the bounded test import/function-name search, so no Windows runtime behavior is claimed.
